name: Microsoft Defender XDR — IOC hunting
description: Advanced hunting queries that look for a list of indicators across Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365 and Defender for Identity tables.

variables.label: Time range
variables.description: Passed to ago(). Advanced hunting keeps 30 days of data.

templates.name: Network connections to the indicators
templates.description: Devices that opened a connection towards the indicators, with the process that initiated it.
templates.body:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Network connections — one line per device
templates.description: Same as above collapsed to a triage table: which device, how many times, first and last seen.
templates.body:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Processes = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10)
          by DeviceName, {{field}}
| sort by Hits desc

templates.name: File hashes seen on endpoints
templates.description: File, process and image load events matching the hashes. Covers dropped files as well as execution.
templates.body:
union DeviceFileEvents, DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, {{field}},
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Executions of the hashes
templates.description: Restricted to process creation, to separate an executed sample from one that was only written to disk.
templates.body:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, {{field}}
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Messages received from the senders
templates.description: Defender for Office 365 delivery outcome for messages coming from the indicators.
templates.body:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromAddress, SenderIPv4,
          RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, ThreatTypes, AuthenticationDetails
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Messages containing the URLs
templates.description: Joins EmailUrlInfo with EmailEvents so you get sender, recipient and delivery action for every message carrying the URL.
templates.body:
EmailUrlInfo
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
    | project NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, Url, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Attachments matching the hashes
templates.description: Which messages delivered a file with one of the hashes, and to whom.
templates.body:
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
    | project NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction
) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, SHA256, DeliveryAction
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Safe Links clicks on the URLs
templates.description: Who actually clicked, and whether the click went through the block page.
templates.body:
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, ActionType, IsClickedThrough, ThreatTypes, NetworkMessageId
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Authentications from the IP addresses
templates.description: On-premises and hybrid logon activity sourced from the indicators.
templates.body:
IdentityLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, AccountDisplayName, DeviceName, LogonType, Application, Protocol, IPAddress, ActionType, FailureReason
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Device logons from the IP addresses
templates.description: Remote logons onto endpoints originating from the indicators — the query to run for a suspected lateral movement source.
templates.body:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountDomain, AccountName, LogonType, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemoteDeviceName, IsLocalAdmin
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Indicators written into the registry
templates.description: Catches C2 addresses and payload URLs stored in registry values by a loader.
templates.body:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc

templates.name: Indicators appearing in a command line
templates.description: Slower but broad: finds indicators passed as arguments to any process, which is how downloaders and exfiltration scripts show up.
templates.body:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago({{var:range}})
| where {{field}} {{op}} ({{iocs}})
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
